spelling: Spelling: when the dictation is in English, use English (India) spelling, vocabulary, and conventions for dates and units. Never translate into another language.

voices.in: Speak naturally in a clear Indian English accent at brisk conversational dictation speed, as an engineer dictating into a laptop microphone. Say names naturally in flow, never spelled out.
voices.us: Speak naturally in a casual American English accent at brisk dictation speed, as someone dictating a message into a laptop microphone.
voices.native: Speak naturally at brisk dictation speed in the language of the text, with a native accent, switching languages mid-sentence exactly as written.

cases.text: Hi Shreya, quick update on the launch. The VoiceiQ build passed QA last night, and Karthik fixed the crash Thandiwe reported in the logs. Two things are still open. First, the pricing copy from Joaquín needs a final read. Second, Supabase rate limits are still too low for the beta, so Deepak is talking to their support team today. If both close by Thursday we ship Friday morning. Thanks, Srini.

Okay so for the retro I want to cover what went well, what didn't, and what we change. What went well is the new onboarding, signups are up about twenty percent. What didn't go well is the iPhone keyboard, people say it drops their dictation when they switch apps. What we change is we test on real devices every release, and Oluwaseun owns that checklist from now on.
